It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and marks the article identified by the articleId path parameter as deleted without physically removing it from the database. Mark an article as deleted in the discussion board system by setting its deleted_at timestamp.

This operation performs a soft deletion of the article record, setting the deleted_at field to the current timestamp. The article is not physically removed from the database but is hidden from public view. This soft-delete pattern preserves the article data to maintain referential integrity with related entities including comments (discussion_board_comments), attached images (discussion_board_article_images), and file attachments (discussion_board_article_files).

Security: This operation requires appropriate authorization. Typically, only the article's original author or moderators with content management permissions can delete articles. The authorization logic ensures users cannot delete articles created by others unless they have elevated moderator privileges.

Data preservation: The soft-delete approach preserves discussion continuity and audit trails. Comments referencing the deleted article remain intact, and the article can potentially be restored by clearing the deleted_at timestamp. The deleted_at field is indexed for efficient filtering of active versus deleted content.

This operation is part of the content lifecycle management workflow. Related operations include creating articles (POST /articles), updating articles (PUT /articles/{articleId}), and retrieving article details (GET /articles/{articleId}). List operations should filter out articles where deleted_at is not null to show only active content.

current.description:
Current page number in the pagination sequence.

Represents the zero-based or one-based index of the current page being returned in the response, depending on the API's pagination convention. This value indicates which page of results the client is currently viewing.

Validation constraints ensure this value cannot be negative. When combined with the limit property, clients can calculate the offset for data retrieval (offset = current * limit for zero-based indexing).

Clients use this value to track their position in paginated result sets and to construct navigation controls for moving between pages.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records returned per page.

Defines the page size constraint that determines how many records are included in a single page of results. This value represents the upper boundary for the number of items in the data array of the paginated response.

The limit controls the balance between response payload size and the number of requests needed to retrieve all data. Smaller limits reduce response size and improve initial load times, while larger limits reduce the total number of requests needed.

Typical limit values range from 10 to 100 depending on the resource type and client requirements. Server-side maximum limits may apply to prevent excessive resource consumption.

records.description:
Total number of records available in the complete dataset.

Represents the absolute count of all records that match the query criteria across all pages, not just the current page. This value is determined by executing a COUNT query against the database with the same filtering conditions applied to the data query.

Clients use this value to calculate the total number of pages available, display total result counts in user interfaces, and determine whether additional pages exist beyond the current page.

When no records match the query criteria, this value will be 0, and the pages property will also be 0, indicating an empty result set.

pages.description:
Total number of pages in the complete paginated dataset.

Calculated as the ceiling of records divided by limit: pages = ceil(records / limit). This represents the total number of pages required to display all available records given the current page size.

The ceiling operation ensures that any remainder records are accounted for in an additional page. For example, with 25 records and a limit of 10, pages would be 3 (10 + 10 + 5).

When records is 0, pages will also be 0. When limit is 0, special handling may be required to avoid division by zero, typically resulting in pages being 0 or 1 depending on implementation.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata structure for paginated API responses.

Provides complete information about the pagination state of a data collection, including the current page position, page size configuration, total record count, and total page count. This structure is embedded in paginated response bodies to enable clients to implement pagination controls and understand the full dataset scope.

The pagination metadata allows clients to calculate navigation targets (first page, last page, next page, previous page) and display user-friendly pagination information such as "Showing 11-20 of 47 results" or "Page 2 of 5".

All numeric values use integer types with non-negative constraints to ensure valid pagination states. The relationship between these properties is mathematically consistent, with pages being derived from records and limit.

access.description:

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

applications.

Clients use this pagination data to build navigation controls (first/previous/next/last page buttons), display result summaries ("Showing 11-20 of 47 members"), and determine whether additional pages exist beyond the current view. The metadata enables proper pagination state management in user interfaces.

The pagination object calculates the total pages based on the configured page size and total matching records, ensuring clients have complete information for implementing efficient member list browsing in administrative and moderation contexts.

data.description:

Contains the actual member data for this page of results, with each element being a lightweight IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary object optimized for list display contexts. The array length will not exceed the pagination limit specified in the request, and may be shorter on the final page or when fewer records match the query criteria.

Each member summary includes essential identification fields (id, username, email), account status information, verification state, and registration timestamp. This curated field set provides sufficient information for rendering member lists in administrative interfaces while excluding sensitive authentication details and verbose profile data.

Clients render this array to display the member list, typically in a table or card layout showing username, status badges, registration dates, and action buttons. For complete member details including all database fields and relationships, clients can fetch individual members using the id from these summaries via dedicated member detail endpoints.

When the search/filter criteria match no members, this array will be empty while the pagination metadata will indicate 0 total records and 0 total pages.

The pagination information enables clients to implement proper page navigation controls and display total record counts.

The data array contains lightweight member summary DTOs optimized for list displays, showing only essential identification information. Full member details can be retrieved by following up with individual member detail requests using the member IDs from the summaries.

The pagination structure allows clients to navigate through session history without loading all records at once, which is critical for members with many active or historical sessions. Each page contains session summary information optimized for session management interfaces, including essential identification details, connection metadata, and creation timestamps.

This paginated response is returned by session search and filtering operations, supporting complex queries based on IP address, user agent, creation date ranges, and other session attributes. The response structure ensures consistent pagination behavior across all session-related endpoints in the discussion board system.

The pagination structure prevents overwhelming clients with large moderator datasets by breaking results into manageable pages. Each page contains moderator summary information optimized for list displays, providing essential identification and profile details without including sensitive authentication data or full moderator profiles.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

This required field captures the IP address of the guest user's connection. The IP address is stored in the session record in the discussion_board_guests table for audit trails and security analysis.

While the server can typically extract this from the request headers in most scenarios, clients must provide it explicitly to ensure the database constraint is satisfied. The IP address enables tracking of guest browsing patterns, security monitoring, and analytics about visitor sources.

Format should be valid IPv4 or IPv6 address. This field is required because the database schema defines it as a non-nullable String field.

href.description:
Current page URL where the guest registration is initiated.

This required field captures the full URL of the page from which the guest user is registering. It represents the connection URL and provides context about the user's entry point into the application. This information is essential for analytics, tracking user journey, and understanding which pages drive guest registration.

Must be a valid URI format representing the complete URL including protocol, domain, and path.

referrer.description:
Previous page URL that led the user to the registration page.

This required field captures the referrer URL, indicating where the guest user came from before initiating registration. It represents the previous page in the user's navigation flow and is crucial for understanding traffic sources and user acquisition channels.

Must be a valid URI format. Can be an empty string if the user accessed the site directly without a referrer.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ICreate.description:
Guest registration request data for creating temporary anonymous accounts.

This DTO represents the minimal information required to register a guest user in the system. Guest registration is designed to be as frictionless as possible, requiring no personal information, email, or password. The primary purpose is to establish a trackable session for anonymous visitors while they browse public content.

The request includes session context fields (ip, href, and referrer) that are mandatory for tracking the guest's connection details, entry point, and navigation flow. These fields enable the system to understand how guests discover and interact with the platform, providing essential analytics and security monitoring capabilities.

Guest accounts created through this DTO are temporary and intended for read-only access. They do not grant posting, commenting, or any write operation privileges. The backend will generate a unique guest identifier and establish a session record in the discussion_board_guests table without requiring authentication credentials.

Unique identifier of the authenticated guest user.

This UUID uniquely identifies the guest account in the discussion_board_guests table. It remains constant throughout the guest's session lifecycle and is embedded in the issued JWT tokens for subsequent authentication.

The guest ID is used to track the guest's activities, manage their session state, and associate any temporary data or preferences with their account during their browsing session.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Response body containing authentication tokens and guest information after successful token refresh.

This DTO is returned when a guest user successfully refreshes their access token using a valid refresh token. It provides the renewed JWT tokens necessary for continued platform access, along with the guest's unique identifier for reference.

The response enables the client to update its stored authentication credentials and continue making authenticated requests without interruption. Both access and refresh tokens may be rotated depending on the system's token rotation policy, ensuring enhanced security through token refresh cycles.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token issued during initial guest registration.

This JWT refresh token was provided when the guest account was created and is used to obtain a new access token without re-registering. The token must be valid, not expired, and associated with an existing guest session in the discussion_board_guests table.

The refresh token has a longer lifetime than access tokens, allowing guests to maintain their session continuity even after the access token expires. The system validates this token's signature, expiration time, and association with an active guest account before issuing new tokens.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing guest user access tokens.

This DTO contains the refresh token required to renew a guest user's access token. Guest users receive both access and refresh tokens when they first register on the platform. When their access token expires, they use this endpoint to exchange their valid refresh token for a new access token, maintaining session continuity without needing to create a new guest account.

The refresh operation is essential for guest user experience, allowing them to continue browsing public content seamlessly. The system validates the provided refresh token against stored session data to ensure it is authentic, unexpired, and associated with a valid guest account.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ICreate.description:
Registration information for creating a new member account.

This type represents the complete set of information required to register a new member on the discussion board platform. It contains the essential credentials and profile information needed to create a new record in the discussion_board_members table.

The registration process validates email uniqueness, password strength, and username availability. Upon successful validation, the system creates a new member account with securely hashed credentials and immediately authenticates the user by issuing JWT tokens.

This type is used exclusively for the member registration endpoint and includes session context fields to enable proper audit trail creation for the initial registration event. The session information is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table to track the registration context.

email.description:
Member's email address for account identification and authentication.

This email must be unique across all members in the discussion_board_members table and serves as the primary authentication identifier. The system validates the email format against RFC 5322 standards and checks for uniqueness before account creation. If the email is already registered, the registration fails with an appropriate error.

password.description:
Member's chosen password for account security.

This is the plain text password provided during registration, which the backend will securely hash before storing in the discussion_board_members table. The password must meet minimum security requirements (typically minimum length and complexity rules). The plain text password is never stored or logged.

username.description:
Member's display name visible to other users on the platform.

This username is the public-facing identifier shown on articles, comments, and throughout the discussion board. It must be unique across all members in the discussion_board_members table and is appropriate for public display. The username is subject to length and character constraints as defined in the Prisma schema validation rules.

ip.description:
Client IP address for registration tracking and security monitoring.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for server-side rendering scenarios. If not provided, the server extracts the IP address from the request headers. This IP address is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table to track the registration origin for audit and security purposes.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the current page where registration is occurring.

Mandatory field containing the full URL of the page from which the registration request originates. This is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table to track user registration locations and enables proper session context for analytics and security monitoring.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL representing the previous page before registration.

Mandatory field containing the URL of the page that the user was on before navigating to the registration page. This can be an empty string for direct access. This information is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table for tracking user acquisition sources and registration context.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated member.

This UUID uniquely identifies the member account in the discussion_board_members table. It serves as the primary reference for the member throughout the system.

username.description:
Member's chosen display name for the discussion board.

Must be unique across all members in the platform. Used for member identification in articles, comments, and throughout the user interface. Subject to length and character constraints as defined in the Prisma schema validation rules.

email.description:
Member's email address for authentication and notifications.

Must be unique across all members. Used as primary credential for login authentication and for sending platform notifications. Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards.

status.description:
Current account status indicating member's access level and restrictions.

This field reflects the moderation state of the member account as defined in the discussion_board_members table. Valid values include: 'active' for full platform access, 'suspended' for temporarily restricted accounts due to moderation actions, and 'locked' for accounts temporarily frozen due to security concerns.

The status determines what operations the member can perform on the platform. Suspended members have limited access, while locked accounts require security verification before access is restored. This field is managed by moderators and automated security systems.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status indicating whether the member has confirmed their email address.

This boolean flag tracks whether the member has completed the email verification process as required by the discussion_board_members table. Members must verify their email before gaining full access to platform features.

Unverified accounts may have restricted functionality until email confirmation is completed. This field is automatically set to false during registration and updated to true when the member clicks the verification link sent to their email address.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account was created.

Records the exact date and time of member registration in ISO 8601 format. Provides audit trail for account creation and helps track platform growth metrics. Automatically set by the system during registration and never modified.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account information was last modified.

Records the exact date and time of the most recent update to the member's account data in ISO 8601 format, as tracked in the discussion_board_members table. This includes changes to profile information, password updates, status modifications, or any other account field updates.

This timestamp is automatically updated by the system whenever any member account data is modified. It provides an audit trail for account changes and helps with data synchronization and cache invalidation strategies.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized.description:
Response body containing authenticated member information and JWT tokens.

This DTO is returned after successful authentication operations including login, registration, and token refresh. It provides the member's identifier and the JWT tokens required for subsequent authenticated API requests.

The access token should be included in the Authorization header of subsequent requests, while the refresh token should be stored securely for token renewal when the access token expires.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for member authentication.

This type represents the information required for an existing member to authenticate with the discussion board platform. It contains the member's registered email address and password, which are validated against the discussion_board_members table to verify identity and grant access.

The password is transmitted in plain text over HTTPS and is compared against the securely hashed password stored in the database. Upon successful validation, the system issues JWT tokens for authenticated session access.

This type is used exclusively for the member login endpoint and represents the minimal credential set required for authentication. It includes session context fields to enable proper audit trail and security monitoring of login activities.

email.description:
Member's registered email address used as the primary authentication identifier.

This email must exactly match an email address registered in the discussion_board_members table. The system performs case-insensitive email matching during authentication. If the email is not found or does not match any registered account, authentication fails.

password.description:
Member's password for authentication verification.

This is the plain text password provided by the user, which the backend validates against the securely hashed password stored in the discussion_board_members table. The password is never stored or logged in plain text form. If the password does not match the stored hash, authentication fails.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

Optional field that can be provided by the client for server-side rendering scenarios. If not provided, the server extracts the IP address from the request headers. This IP address is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table for audit trail and security purposes.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the current page where login is occurring.

Mandatory field containing the full URL of the page from which the login request originates. This is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table to track user login locations and enables proper session context for security monitoring and analytics.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL representing the previous page before login.

Mandatory field containing the URL of the page that the user was on before navigating to the login page. This can be an empty string for direct access. This information is stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table for tracking user navigation patterns and session context.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token obtained from a previous authentication response.

This token is used to request new access and refresh tokens without requiring the member to re-enter their credentials. The refresh token must be valid and not expired.

The token is validated against the discussion_board_member_sessions table to ensure it belongs to an active session. If the token is invalid, expired, or associated with a terminated session, the refresh operation will fail.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing member authentication tokens.

This DTO contains the refresh token that was previously issued during login or registration. The refresh token is exchanged for a new set of authentication tokens (access token and refresh token) to maintain continuous authenticated access without requiring re-authentication.

The refresh operation validates the provided token against active member sessions and ensures the token has not expired or been revoked.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description:
Moderator registration data for creating new accounts.

This type defines the request body structure for moderator registration (join) operations. It contains all necessary information to create a new moderator account in the discussion_board_moderators table.

The registration process validates the provided data, ensures email uniqueness, hashes the password securely, and creates both the moderator account and an initial authentication session. The system automatically generates the account ID and timestamps during creation.

This type includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that capture the connection metadata for the initial registration event. These fields are stored in the moderator session record to maintain an audit trail of account creation circumstances.

email.description:
Moderator's email address for the new account.

This must be a unique, valid email address not already registered in the system. Email validation ensures proper RFC 5322 format, and uniqueness checks prevent duplicate accounts. This email becomes the primary authentication identifier and is used for account recovery and notifications.

password.description:
Moderator's password for the new account.

This plain-text password is provided during registration and will be securely hashed using industry-standard algorithms (such as bcrypt or Argon2) before storage in the database. Password strength requirements should be enforced to ensure adequate security for administrative accounts.

username.description:
Unique username for the moderator account.

This username serves as both the authentication identifier and the display name for the moderator. It must be unique across all moderators in the discussion board system. The username is used for login operations and is displayed when moderators perform moderation actions, ensuring accountability and transparency in community management.

This field corresponds to the 'username' column in the discussion_board_moderators Prisma schema.

ip.description:
Client IP address for initial session tracking.

This optional field captures the IP address from which the registration request originates. While the server can extract this from request headers, clients may provide it explicitly for server-side rendering scenarios. The IP is stored in the initial moderator session record for security auditing.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) where registration is occurring.

This required field captures the full URL of the registration page. It provides context about where the moderator signed up and helps track registration sources. This information is stored in the initial session record and can be used for analytics and registration flow optimization.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) before registration page.

This required field captures the URL of the page the user was on before navigating to the registration page. It helps understand how users discover the moderator registration option and can be used to optimize onboarding flows. Can be an empty string for direct access to the registration page.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description:
Successful authentication response for moderators.

This DTO represents the complete authentication result returned after successful login or token refresh operations. It contains the moderator's identity information and authentication tokens required for subsequent API requests.

The response includes both access and refresh tokens following JWT standards. The access token is short-lived and used for API authentication, while the refresh token enables obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

This response structure is used across all moderator authentication flows including initial login and token refresh operations, providing consistent authentication credentials throughout the moderator's session.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key in the discussion_board_moderators table and uniquely identifies the moderator account across the system. Used for authorization checks and associating moderation actions with specific moderator accounts.

username.description:
Moderator's unique username for authentication and display.

The username serves as both the authentication identifier and the public display name for the moderator. It must be unique across all moderators in the system. This field is used for login operations and is displayed when moderators perform moderation actions, ensuring accountability and transparency in community management.

email.description:
Moderator's email address for notifications and account recovery.

Valid email address used for system notifications, password recovery, and official communications. Must be unique across all moderators and conform to RFC 5322 email format standards. The email serves as a secondary authentication factor and critical communication channel for administrative purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when this moderator account was first registered in the system. This field is automatically set by the database on record creation and is immutable. It provides important audit trail information and helps track the history of moderator accounts in the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the moderator account.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when any field in the moderator record was last modified. This field is automatically updated by the database whenever the record changes. It supports audit trails, cache invalidation strategies, and helps track the evolution of moderator profiles over time.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description:
Moderator login credentials for authentication.

This type defines the request body structure for moderator login operations. It contains the essential credentials needed to authenticate an existing moderator account and establish an authenticated session.

The login process validates these credentials against stored moderator records in the discussion_board_moderators table. The password is compared against the hashed password stored in the database using secure comparison algorithms. Upon successful validation, the system generates JWT tokens and creates a session record.

This type includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that capture connection metadata for security auditing and session tracking purposes. These fields help identify the source of login attempts and maintain detailed authentication logs for security monitoring.

email.description:
Moderator's email address for authentication.

This must match the email registered with an existing moderator account. The system performs a case-insensitive lookup to locate the corresponding account in the discussion_board_moderators table. Email format validation ensures proper structure before authentication attempt.

password.description:

This is the plain-text password provided by the moderator during login. The backend securely compares this against the hashed password stored in the database using constant-time comparison algorithms to prevent timing attacks. The password is never stored or logged in plain text.

ip.description:

href.description:

This required field captures the full URL of the page where the moderator initiated the login. It provides context about the login entry point and helps track user flows. This information is stored in the session record and can be used for analytics and security monitoring.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) before login page.

This required field captures the URL of the page the moderator was on before navigating to the login page. It helps understand user navigation patterns and can be used to redirect users back to their intended destination after successful authentication. Can be an empty string for direct access to the login page.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for moderator authentication.

This DTO contains the refresh token required to obtain new access tokens without re-entering credentials. The refresh token must be valid, non-expired, and associated with an active moderator session in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table.

The refresh token is validated against the session record to ensure it hasn't been revoked, the session is still active, and the associated moderator account remains in good standing. This enables secure token rotation while maintaining continuous authenticated access.

Used exclusively in token refresh operations where moderators need to extend their session without full re-authentication.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token issued during initial authentication.

This token is validated against the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to verify authenticity, check expiration status, and confirm association with an active moderator account. Must be a valid JWT token that hasn't been revoked or expired.

The refresh token enables secure session extension without requiring the moderator to re-enter credentials, balancing security through short-lived access tokens with usability through longer-lived refresh tokens.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for retrieving discussion board members.

This DTO defines the query parameters for filtering, searching, sorting, and paginating through the discussion board member list. It supports comprehensive member discovery and management capabilities for authorized users (moderators and administrators).

The request enables flexible member searches through username pattern matching, email filtering, registration date range filtering, and account status filtering. Pagination controls ensure efficient data retrieval for large member bases, while sorting options provide customizable result ordering.

Used exclusively in member list operations where moderators need to find and manage registered users. All search and filter operations are performed against the discussion_board_members table.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to return, with page numbering starting at 1. Combined with limit to implement offset-based pagination. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

For example, with limit=20, page=1 returns records 1-20, page=2 returns records 21-40, etc.

limit.description:

Controls the page size for pagination, with a maximum limit to prevent excessive data transfer. Defaults to a reasonable value (typically 20-50) if not specified.

For example, searching 'john' would match 'john_doe', 'JohnSmith', 'alice_johnson', etc. Empty or omitted search returns all members (subject to other filters).

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary.description:

IDiscussionBoardMember.description:
Registered member entity in the discussion board system.

Represents a user who has completed registration and can actively participate in economic and political discussions. Members can author articles, post comments, and engage with other community members. This entity tracks core member identity information, account metadata, and registration status.

Contains modifiable fields that members can update in their own profiles. All fields are optional as members may choose to update only specific aspects of their profile in a single operation. The update operation enforces business rules such as username uniqueness validation.

This field is essential for database-level operations, direct relationship queries, and scenarios where only the member identifier is needed without deserializing the full member object. member.description:

This information is displayed to members to help them verify legitimate access.

href.description:
Connection URL where the session was initiated.

This field captures the full URL of the page from which the member established this authentication session. It helps track the entry point of the session and can be used for analytics and security monitoring to understand user authentication patterns and detect unusual authentication flows.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the member came from when starting the session.

This field contains the URL of the page that directed the user to establish this session. It captures the HTTP Referer header value and provides context about how the user arrived at the authentication flow. This information is useful for tracking user navigation patterns and identifying potential phishing attempts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created (login time).

This field records the exact date and time when the member successfully authenticated and the session was established. It is set automatically by the system during session creation and is immutable. The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format and helps members identify when they logged in from each device.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated.

This field records when the session ended, either through natural expiration, explicit logout, or administrative termination. A null value indicates an active session that has not yet expired. The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format.

This field is crucial for session lifecycle management, enabling the system to distinguish between active and terminated sessions. It supports security features like automatic session cleanup, inactive session detection, and session history tracking.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.description:
Complete member authentication session entity with all security-relevant details.

This schema represents a full authentication session record for a discussion board member, containing all information necessary for session management, security monitoring, and member account protection. It includes session identification, complete member context, network information, connection context, and temporal data.

The session entity is used in detailed session retrieval operations where members need comprehensive information to verify the legitimacy of their login sessions. It provides all data points required for members to identify unauthorized access attempts, including IP addresses, connection URLs, session timestamps, and complete member details for each session.

Security considerations include strict access control ensuring members can only view their own session details, with moderators having elevated permissions for security investigations. The complete session data enables robust security monitoring and helps members maintain control over their account access across multiple devices and locations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member session.

This UUID serves as the primary key for session tracking and management. Generated automatically when a member logs in or a new session is established.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Foreign key identifier of the member who owns this session.

This UUID references the discussion_board_members.id field, representing the database-level foreign key relationship defined in the Prisma schema. Provides direct access to the member identifier for authorization checks, relationship queries, and database operations without requiring deserialization of the full member object.

member.description:
The discussion board member associated with this session.

Provides complete context about the authenticated user whose session this represents. Includes essential member identification information for session validation and user context.

ip.description:
IP address from which the session was initiated.

Records the client's IP address for security monitoring and audit trails. Used for detecting suspicious login patterns and enforcing security policies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Used for session expiration calculations and activity tracking.

expired_at.description:

This field is essential for session management interfaces where users need to see which sessions are currently active versus already terminated. Enables filtering and sorting of session lists by status.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of a member authentication session for session management contexts.

This summary type provides essential session information including the associated member context and session status. Optimized for scenarios where session validation or user context lookup is needed without retrieving full session details.

Used in authentication flows, session validation middleware, user activity tracking, and session management interfaces. Provides sufficient information to identify the active user, basic session metadata, and session status while maintaining efficient payload sizes.

page.description:

Specifies which page of session results to retrieve. Page numbering starts at 1. Used in conjunction with limit to implement offset-based pagination for large session lists.

This field controls the offset in the result set, enabling efficient navigation through multiple pages of member authentication sessions.

limit.description:
Number of session records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Must be between 1 and 100 to prevent excessive data retrieval and maintain optimal server performance.

A reasonable default would be 20-50 sessions per page for optimal user experience. This limit ensures manageable payload sizes while providing sufficient context for session management.

oneOf.description:
Sort by session creation time in ascending order (oldest first).

Orders sessions from oldest to newest based on the created_at timestamp field from the Prisma schema. Useful for reviewing session history chronologically or analyzing login patterns over time.

Sort by session creation time in descending order (newest first).

Orders sessions from newest to oldest based on the created_at timestamp field from the Prisma schema. This is the recommended default sort order for security monitoring, as it shows the most recent login activity first.

sort.description:
Sort order for session results based on Prisma schema fields.

Determines how sessions are ordered in the response. Sorting options are tied directly to the discussion_board_member_sessions table structure.

The default sort order should be '-created_at' to show most recent sessions first, which is typically most useful for security monitoring and identifying current active sessions.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by IP address.

When provided, returns only sessions created from the specified IP address. This field corresponds to the ip column in the discussion_board_member_sessions Prisma schema.

Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats. Useful for members wanting to review all sessions from a specific network location or for identifying potential unauthorized access from particular IP addresses.

href.description:
Filter sessions by connection URL.

When provided, returns only sessions where the href field matches or contains this value. The href field in the Prisma schema represents the connection URL where the session was initiated.

Useful for identifying sessions created from specific application pages or entry points. Supports substring matching to find sessions from particular sections of the application.

referrer.description:
Filter sessions by referrer URL.

When provided, returns only sessions where the referrer field matches or contains this value. The referrer field in the Prisma schema indicates where the member came from when starting the session.

Helps identify sessions originating from specific sources, external links, or marketing campaigns. Supports substring matching for flexible filtering.

created_after.description:
Filter sessions created after this timestamp.

When provided, returns only sessions where the created_at field in the Prisma schema is after the specified date and time. Used for date range filtering to help members review sessions from specific time periods.

Must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Enables temporal analysis of login patterns and security monitoring for specific time windows.

created_before.description:
Filter sessions created before this timestamp.

When provided, returns only sessions where the created_at field in the Prisma schema is before the specified date and time. Used in combination with created_after to define specific date ranges for session review.

Must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Supports historical session analysis and audit trail reviews.

expired_at_is_null.description:
Filter sessions by expiration status.

When true, returns only active sessions (where expired_at field in Prisma schema is null). When false, returns only expired or terminated sessions (where expired_at is not null).

The expired_at field in the discussion_board_member_sessions table indicates when a session was terminated. Null values represent currently active sessions, while non-null values indicate the session has ended.

This filter is crucial for security monitoring, allowing members to distinguish between their active login sessions and historical terminated sessions.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for retrieving member authentication sessions.

This schema defines the request parameters for searching and filtering a member's authentication sessions from the discussion_board_member_sessions Prisma table. It supports comprehensive filtering options that directly align with the database schema fields including pagination controls, sorting preferences, IP address filtering, URL-based filtering (href and referrer), temporal filtering with date ranges, and session status filtering.

The request schema enables members to effectively manage their session security by providing flexible search capabilities tied to actual session data. Members can search for sessions from specific locations (IP), entry points (href), referral sources (referrer), time periods (created_at ranges), or activity status (expired_at).

All filter parameters are optional, allowing for both broad session listing (no filters) and highly targeted searches (multiple filters combined). The pagination parameters ensure efficient retrieval of large session lists without overwhelming the client or server.

Security consideration: This request DTO is used with operations that have authorizationActor='member', ensuring members can only query their own sessions through proper server-side authorization.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request parameters for retrieving discussion board moderators.

This schema defines the query parameters for searching and filtering moderators in the discussion board system. It supports advanced search capabilities including text-based search across moderator attributes, status filtering, date range queries, and flexible sorting options.

The request schema enables administrators to find specific moderators based on various criteria such as username, email, account status, or registration dates. Pagination controls ensure efficient data retrieval for large moderator datasets.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Page numbering starts at 1 for the first page. Combined with limit parameter to control result set windows.

Default value is typically 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Maximum number of moderator records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, limiting how many moderator records are included in a single response. The system enforces a maximum limit to prevent excessive data retrieval and maintain performance.

Typical default values range from 20 to 50 records per page.

search.description:
General search term for finding moderators.

Performs text-based search across multiple moderator fields including username and email. The search is typically case-insensitive and may support partial matching to help users find moderators even with incomplete information.

Useful for quick moderator lookups when the exact identifier is unknown.

sort.description:
Field name to sort results by.

Specifies which moderator attribute should be used for ordering the result set. Common sort fields include created_at for chronological ordering, username for alphabetical sorting, or email for contact-based organization.

The sort direction is controlled by the separate order parameter.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort order.

Arranges results from lowest to highest value based on the field specified in the sort parameter. For alphabetical fields like username or email, this means A-Z ordering. For date fields like created_at or updated_at, this means oldest to newest (chronological order).

Use ascending order when you want to see earliest records first, alphabetically first items, or numerically smallest values at the top of the result set.

Descending sort order.

Arranges results from highest to lowest value based on the field specified in the sort parameter. For alphabetical fields like username or email, this means Z-A ordering. For date fields like created_at or updated_at, this means newest to oldest (reverse chronological order).

Use descending order when you want to see most recent records first, alphabetically last items, or numerically largest values at the top of the result set. This is typically the default for date-based sorting to show the latest activity first.

order.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Determines whether results are sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the field specified in the sort parameter.

Ascending order arranges items from lowest to highest (A-Z, oldest to newest), while descending order arranges from highest to lowest (Z-A, newest to oldest).

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description:
Lightweight moderator representation for references and associations.

Provides essential moderator information used when moderator context is needed in other entities (such as sessions, moderation actions, or article management). Contains just enough information to identify the moderator and display basic profile details without the overhead of the complete moderator entity.

Used extensively as a reference type when other entities need to include moderator context, such as showing who performed a moderation action or which moderator owns a session. This summary representation prevents circular references and keeps response payloads efficient.

Excludes sensitive information like authentication details (password_hash) and includes only public-facing or administratively relevant moderator attributes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator.

System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this moderator account across the platform. Used for moderator references in sessions, moderation logs, and administrative operations.

email.description:
Moderator email address for authentication and administrative communication.

Serves as a primary contact method for administrative notifications and account-related communications. Must be unique across all moderators in the system to ensure proper identification and prevent duplicate accounts.

This email is used for authentication purposes and administrative correspondence, making it a critical field for moderator account management and security operations.

username.description:
Moderator's unique username.

Human-readable identifier used for moderator attribution in moderation actions and administrative interfaces. Must be unique across all moderators in the system.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

Provides context about moderator tenure, useful for understanding moderator experience level and account age in administrative dashboards.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account information was last modified.

Tracks the most recent update to any moderator profile field, providing audit trail information for account changes. This timestamp is automatically updated by the system whenever profile modifications occur, helping administrators monitor account activity and verify recent changes.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying an existing moderator's profile information.

This DTO defines the editable fields that can be modified when updating a moderator account. It follows the partial update pattern where all fields are optional, allowing clients to update only the specific attributes they wish to change without affecting other fields.

The update operation typically supports self-service profile management where moderators can update their own information. Common update scenarios include changing username, updating contact email, or modifying other profile details.

Security constraints apply to this operation. The moderator's unique code and internal ID are immutable and cannot be changed through updates. Password changes should be handled through dedicated password change endpoints with additional security verification. Creation and update timestamps are system-managed and excluded from client updates. Authorization checks ensure moderators can only update their own profiles unless they have elevated administrative privileges.

username.description:
Updated username for the moderator account.

Optional field allowing moderators to change their display name and authentication identifier. The new username must be unique across all moderators in the system. Username changes should be carefully considered as they affect how the moderator is identified in moderation logs and community interactions.

email.description:
Updated email address for the moderator account.

Optional field for changing the moderator's contact email. The new email must be unique across all moderators and conform to valid email format standards (RFC 5322). Email changes may trigger verification workflows to confirm ownership of the new address before the change is finalized.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.description:
Complete moderator entity representation for the discussion board system.

This entity represents authenticated moderators who maintain community standards and manage the discussion board platform. Moderators have elevated privileges to review content, manage users, enforce community guidelines, and perform administrative tasks.

Moderators are identified by an internal UUID for system integrity. Each moderator maintains a user profile with contact information and authentication credentials. The entity tracks creation and modification timestamps for audit purposes.

This type is used in detailed retrieval responses and administrative operations where complete moderator information is required. Sensitive authentication data (password hash) is excluded from this response representation for security purposes.

id.description:
Unique internal identifier for the moderator entity.

System-generated UUID that serves as the primary key in the database. This identifier is immutable and used for internal referencing and data integrity. It ensures global uniqueness across the entire system and supports distributed database architectures.

email.description:
Moderator's email address for notifications and account recovery.

Valid email address used for system notifications, password recovery, and official communications. Must be unique across all moderators and conform to RFC 5322 email format standards. The email serves as a secondary authentication factor and critical communication channel for administrative purposes.

password_hash.description:
Hashed password for moderator authentication.

Securely hashed representation of the moderator's password using bcrypt algorithm with a minimum cost factor of 10. This field stores the cryptographic hash of the actual password, never the plaintext password itself, ensuring security even if the database is compromised.

The password hash is used during authentication to verify moderator credentials by comparing the hash of the provided password with this stored value. This field is critical for secure authentication and must be protected with appropriate access controls and never exposed in API responses.

username.description:
Moderator's unique username for authentication and display.

The username serves as both the authentication identifier and the public display name for the moderator. It must be unique across all moderators in the system. This field is used for login operations and is displayed when moderators perform moderation actions, ensuring accountability and transparency in community management.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when this moderator account was first registered in the system. This field is automatically set by the database on record creation and is immutable. It provides important audit trail information and helps track the history of moderator accounts in the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the moderator account.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when any field in the moderator record was last modified. This field is automatically updated by the database whenever the record changes. It supports audit trails, cache invalidation strategies, and helps track the evolution of moderator profiles over time.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.description:
Complete moderator authentication session entity.

Represents an active authentication session for a moderator account in the discussion board system. Each session is created when a moderator successfully logs in and contains the session identifier, creation timestamp, expiration details, and connection metadata.

Sessions are the primary mechanism for maintaining authenticated state for moderators across the platform. Each session links to a specific moderator account through the discussion_board_moderator_id foreign key and tracks the authentication lifecycle from creation to expiration or explicit logout.

This entity corresponds to the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table in the Prisma schema. Sessions enable secure, stateful authentication without requiring moderators to re-enter credentials for each request. The session record serves as proof of authentication and is validated on each API request to protected endpoints.

Used in session retrieval responses, logout operations, and authentication flows. Contains connection metadata that must be transmitted securely and protected with appropriate access controls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator session.

System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this authentication session across the entire platform. This ID is used for session lookup, deletion, and management operations.

Generated automatically by the database upon session creation and remains immutable throughout the session's lifecycle.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description:
Reference to the moderator who owns this session.

Foreign key linking this session to the specific moderator account in the discussion_board_moderators table. This relationship establishes which moderator is authenticated through this session and is critical for authorization and access control.

This field corresponds to the discussion_board_moderator_id column in the Prisma schema and enables efficient querying of all sessions belonging to a specific moderator. Used in session management operations, security auditing, and implementing features like 'logout from all devices'.

ip.description:
IP address from which the moderator established this session.

Records the client's IP address at the time of session creation for security auditing and monitoring purposes. This field enables detection of suspicious login patterns, geographic anomalies, and potential account compromise scenarios.

The IP address is captured during the authentication process and remains immutable for the session's lifetime. Used in security dashboards, fraud detection systems, and compliance reporting to track where moderator authentication requests originate.

href.description:
Connection URL where the session was initiated.

Captures the full URL of the page or endpoint where the moderator initiated the login process. This connection metadata provides context about how and where the authentication occurred.

Useful for analytics, debugging authentication flows, and understanding user behavior patterns. Combined with referrer data, this field helps reconstruct the complete authentication journey and identify potential security issues or UX problems in the login flow.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the moderator came from when starting the session.

Records the HTTP referrer header value that indicates which page or external source directed the moderator to the login page. This metadata helps track authentication flow origins and user navigation patterns.

Provides valuable context for security analysis (detecting phishing attempts), marketing analytics (understanding traffic sources), and UX optimization (improving authentication funnels). An empty string indicates direct navigation to the login page.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

Records the exact moment when the moderator successfully authenticated and this session was established. Used for session age calculations, security auditing, and determining when sessions should expire.

Automatically set by the database upon session creation and remains immutable throughout the session's lifecycle.

expired_at.description:

Records when the session ended, either through natural expiration based on timeout policies, explicit logout by the moderator, or forced termination by system administrators. A null value indicates an active session that has not yet expired.

This field is critical for session lifecycle management, security compliance (ensuring inactive sessions are terminated), and audit trails. Used to implement automatic session cleanup, detect abandoned sessions, and enforce security policies around maximum session duration.

When a moderator logs out or a session times out, this field is set to the current timestamp, marking the session as inactive and preventing further use of the associated session.

moderator.description:
Summary information about the moderator who owns this session.

Provides contextual information about the authenticated moderator, including their identifier, username, and basic profile details. This reference allows session information to be displayed alongside moderator context without requiring separate API calls.

Transformed from the discussion_board_moderator_id foreign key to provide complete moderator context in a single response.
