Sorting capabilities allow ordering by publication date, popularity (view count), or last update time, in either ascending or descending order. Pagination parameters enable efficient navigation through large result sets while maintaining reasonable response sizes and server performance.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Article creation request data for publishing new discussion board articles.

This type defines the required data that authenticated members must provide when creating new articles for economic and political discussions. It contains only the user-provided content fields (title and body), excluding system-managed metadata which is automatically generated.

Critical security principle: The author identity (discussion_board_member_id) and authentication session (discussion_board_member_session_id) are NEVER accepted from the request body. These values are automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and injected by the backend to prevent impersonation attacks and ensure authentic attribution.

Content validation requirements enforce quality standards: titles must be 5-200 characters (concise yet descriptive), and body content must be 10-50,000 characters (substantial discussions without abuse). Rich text formatting is supported in the body field for comprehensive economic and political discussions.

System-managed fields excluded from this request type include: id (auto-generated UUID), view_count (initialized to 0), created_at and updated_at (set to current timestamp), and deleted_at (initialized to null). These are handled automatically by the backend during the article creation process.

The operation enforces authentication to ensure only registered members can create articles, and implements rate limiting to prevent spam posting. Content validation ensures proper formatting and length constraints before database persistence.

title.description:
Article title summarizing the topic or main argument.

The headline or subject of the article, must be between 5 and 200 characters to ensure meaningful yet concise titles. Should be descriptive enough to convey the article's main topic and attract readers interested in economic and political discussions.

This title will be displayed in article listings, search results, and as the page heading when viewing the full article. It corresponds to the title column in the discussion_board_articles table.

body.description:
Full article content containing the member's analysis, arguments, and discussion points.

The main content of the article supporting rich text formatting including paragraphs and line breaks for comprehensive economic and political discussions. Must be between 10 and 50,000 characters to ensure substantive content while preventing abuse.

This field should contain the complete discussion, analysis, supporting arguments, and any relevant information the author wishes to share. It corresponds to the body column in the discussion_board_articles table with full rich text support.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article.

Primary key used to reference this specific article throughout the system.
Generated automatically upon article creation.

title.description:
Title of the article.

The headline or subject of the discussion topic.
Provides immediate context about the article's subject matter for readers browsing the discussion board.

view_count.description:
Number of times the article has been viewed.

Automatic tracking counter that increments each time the article is successfully retrieved. Provides engagement metrics in list views, enabling sorting by popularity and identifying trending discussions.

Displayed in article listings to help users gauge community interest and article reach. Used for ranking and filtering articles by engagement level.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the article was created.

Records the exact date and time when this article was first published.
Used for chronological sorting, recent activity tracking, and displaying publication dates.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent edit to the article.

Indicates when the article was last modified by the author or a moderator. Helps users identify recently edited content in list views and understand content freshness.

Useful for sorting by recent updates and displaying edit history context without loading full article details.

author.description:
The member who authored this article.

Provides essential information about the article's author including their identity.
Allows displaying author attribution alongside the article in list views without additional API calls.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board article for list views and embedded references.

This lightweight DTO provides essential article information optimized for list displays, search results, and embedded references. It contains the core identifying and display information including engagement metrics (view_count) and update timestamps without the full article body content or associated files.

Used in scenarios where articles are displayed:
- In article listing pages showing multiple articles with sorting by popularity or recency
- In search results matching user queries
- As parent context in comment displays
- In user activity feeds showing their posted articles
- In navigation breadcrumbs and related article links

The summary includes view_count for engagement-based sorting and filtering, and updated_at to identify recently edited content. It excludes the full article body, image attachments, and file attachments to maintain optimal performance in list operations.

For complete article details including full content and attachments, use the main IDiscussionBoardArticle type.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Complete discussion board article entity representing articles published by members for economic and political discussions.

This type represents the full article data structure including all content, metadata, and author information. It is returned from read operations such as retrieving article details (GET /articles/{articleId}) and after successful create/update operations.

The article entity contains the core content (title and body), tracking metadata (view count, timestamps), author association, and soft deletion support. The author field transforms the database foreign key relationship into a complete member summary object, enabling atomic read operations where all article context is retrieved in a single API call without requiring additional requests for author details.

Articles are immediately published and visible to all users upon creation. The system automatically manages view counts, creation/update timestamps, and deletion status. Session tracking for audit trails is maintained internally in the database but not exposed via the API response to keep implementation details private.

Related entities include article images (discussion_board_article_images) and file attachments (discussion_board_article_files) which enrich articles with visual and documentary supporting content. The article serves as the primary discussion entity with associated comments (discussion_board_comments) enabling community interaction.

Security context: Articles are publicly readable by all users including guests. Author information is included to provide attribution and context. The deleted_at field supports soft deletion for content moderation while preserving referential integrity with related entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article.

System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this article across the entire discussion board platform. This identifier is immutable and used for all article references, URL paths, and relationship mappings.

title.description:
Article title.

The headline or subject of the article, constrained to 5-200 characters. Must be concise yet descriptive enough to convey the article's main topic. Used in article listings, search results, and as the page title when viewing the article.

body.description:
Article body content with rich text formatting.

The main content of the article supporting rich text formatting for economic and political discussions. Constrained to 10-50,000 characters to ensure substantial content while preventing abuse. Contains the full discussion, analysis, arguments, and supporting information.

view_count.description:
Number of times the article has been viewed.

Automatic tracking counter that increments each time the article is successfully retrieved. Initialized to 0 upon creation. Provides engagement metrics and helps identify popular content. Used for sorting and ranking in article lists.

created_at.description:
Article creation timestamp.

ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the article was originally published. System-managed field automatically set upon creation. Used for sorting articles chronologically and displaying publication dates. Immutable after creation.

updated_at.description:
Article last modification timestamp.

ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the article was most recently updated. System-managed field automatically updated whenever the article content or metadata changes. Helps users identify recently edited content and track content evolution.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp.

ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the article was soft deleted, or null if the article is active. Supports soft deletion pattern to preserve referential integrity with related entities (comments, attachments) and maintain audit trails. Articles with non-null deleted_at are hidden from public view but remain in the database.

author.description:
The member who authored this article.

Provides complete information about the article's author including their identity, username, email, account status, and registration details. This field transforms the discussion_board_member_id foreign key relationship from the Prisma schema into a full member summary object.

Enables atomic read operations where clients receive complete article context including author details in a single API call, eliminating the need for additional GET /members/:id requests. Essential for displaying author attribution, reputation, and account status alongside article content.

The author relationship is immutable once the article is created, ensuring permanent attribution and ownership tracking. Moderators can use author information to identify content patterns, enforce community standards, and manage member contributions effectively.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Article update request data for modifying existing discussion board articles.

This type defines the optional fields that can be updated on existing articles. It follows the Partial pattern where all fields are optional, allowing clients to update only specific properties without affecting others. Updates are restricted to the article's content fields - ownership and system metadata cannot be modified.

Critical immutability rules: The author identity (discussion_board_member_id) and authentication session (discussion_board_member_session_id) are permanently immutable and excluded from updates to preserve article ownership and attribution integrity. The creation timestamp (created_at) is also immutable as a historical record.

System-managed fields excluded from updates include: id (immutable identifier), updated_at (automatically set to current timestamp by backend), deleted_at (managed through dedicated soft-delete operation), and view_count (automatically incremented on article retrieval).

Authorization enforcement: Members can only update their own articles - the backend verifies that the authenticated member's ID matches the article's discussion_board_member_id. Moderators with elevated privileges can update any article for content moderation purposes. The authorization logic prevents users from modifying articles created by others unless they have moderator privileges.

Content validation: Updated title and body fields must still meet the same constraints as creation (title: 5-200 characters, body: 10-50,000 characters). The operation preserves data integrity by validating all input fields according to schema constraints before persisting changes.

title.description:
Updated article title.

Optional new title for the article, must be 5-200 characters if provided. Should be concise yet descriptive enough to convey the article's main topic. When updated, this becomes the new headline used in article listings and page titles.

body.description:
Updated article body content.

Optional new body content supporting rich text formatting. Must be 10-50,000 characters if provided. When updated, this replaces the existing article content while the updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect the modification time.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.description:
Complete image attachment entity with all metadata and relationship information.

Represents a visual content attachment associated with a discussion board article. Each image serves as supporting material for economic and political discussions, enriching articles with visual context, charts, diagrams, or illustrative photos.

The entity maintains a parent-child relationship with articles through the discussion_board_article_id foreign key, where each image belongs to exactly one article but articles can have multiple images. This supports comprehensive visual documentation of discussion topics.

Includes essential file metadata (original_filename, file_size, content_type, storage_url) and optional enrichment data (width, height dimensions). The storage_url field points to the actual image file stored in external cloud storage or CDN, separating file storage concerns from database operations.

Supports soft deletion through the deleted_at timestamp, allowing images to be marked as removed while preserving audit trails and referential integrity. Soft-deleted images are hidden from public view but retained in the database for recovery and compliance purposes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the image attachment record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the discussion_board_article_images table and uniquely identifies each image attachment across the entire system. Generated automatically by the system upon image creation.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent article.

Establishes the relationship between this image attachment and its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. Each image belongs to exactly one article, while articles can have multiple image attachments.

original_filename.description:
Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

Preserved for user reference and download purposes. This is the actual filename from the user's file system at upload time. May contain file extension indicating image format such as .jpg, .png, .gif, or .webp.

file_size.description:
Size of the image file in bytes.

Used for storage tracking and enforcing the 10 MB maximum file size limit as specified in the Prisma schema description. Must be positive integer value. Helps with storage quota management and performance optimization.

content_type.description:
MIME type of the image file for proper browser rendering.

Valid values include image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp corresponding to supported image formats. Used by browsers and clients to determine how to handle and display the image file.

storage_url.description:
URL or storage path where the image file is stored.

Used by the system to retrieve and serve the image to users viewing the article. May be CDN URL for optimized content delivery or internal cloud storage path. Points to the actual binary image file in external storage infrastructure.

width.description:
Width of the image in pixels.

Captured during upload for display optimization and layout calculations. Used for responsive image sizing and aspect ratio preservation. Null if dimensions could not be determined during upload process.

height.description:
Height of the image in pixels.

Captured during upload for display optimization and layout calculations. Used for responsive image sizing and aspect ratio preservation. Null if dimensions could not be determined during upload process.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system.

Tracks upload time for audit trail and chronological ordering of attachments. Automatically set by the system upon image creation. Follows ISO 8601 date-time format.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was soft deleted.

Null if the image is currently active. Enables recovery and audit trail before permanent removal from storage. When set, indicates the image has been soft-deleted and should be hidden from public view while preserving the database record for audit trail purposes.

original_filename.description:
Original filename of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

This preserves the exact filename that the user specified when uploading the image file. It is maintained for user reference, download purposes, and audit trails. The filename typically includes the file extension indicating the image format (e.g., 'photo.jpg', 'chart.png').

This field is distinct from any display name or title that might be assigned to the image for presentation purposes in the user interface.

file_size.description:
Size of the image file in bytes.

Specifies the exact file size used for storage tracking and enforcing the 10 MB maximum file size limit per image attachment. This value represents the actual binary size of the uploaded image file.

Must be a positive integer value. The system validates this against configured size limits to prevent excessive storage usage and ensure reasonable upload times.

content_type.description:
MIME type of the image file for proper browser rendering.

Specifies the standard MIME type that identifies the image format and enables browsers to handle and display the image correctly. Valid values include:

- image/jpeg (for JPEG/JPG images)
- image/png (for PNG images)
- image/gif (for GIF images)
- image/webp (for WebP images)

This field corresponds to the Content-Type header that will be used when serving the image to clients. The system validates that the content type matches one of the supported image formats.

storage_url.description:
URL or storage path where the image file is stored.

Complete URL reference pointing to the location where the actual image file has been uploaded and stored. This may be a CDN URL for optimized delivery or an internal storage path for direct access.

The image file must be uploaded to storage separately before creating this database record. This URL is then used by the system to retrieve and serve the image to users viewing the article. The URL should be accessible and point to a valid image resource that matches the specified content_type.

width.description:
Width of the image in pixels.

Optional dimension metadata indicating the horizontal size of the image. When provided, this information is captured during upload and used for display optimization and layout calculations in the user interface.

Can be null if the image dimensions could not be determined at upload time or if dimension information is not available. Providing accurate dimensions helps optimize responsive image display and layout rendering.

height.description:
Height of the image in pixels.

Optional dimension metadata indicating the vertical size of the image. When provided, this information is captured during upload and used for display optimization and layout calculations in the user interface.

Can be null if the image dimensions could not be determined at upload time or if dimension information is not available. Providing accurate dimensions helps optimize responsive image display and layout rendering.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new image attachment for a discussion board article.

Contains the essential metadata required to register a new image attachment in the discussion_board_article_images table. This DTO follows the two-phase file handling pattern: first, the actual image file is uploaded to external storage (cloud storage or CDN) which returns a storage URL; second, this metadata is submitted to create the database record linking the image to its parent article.

Required fields include the original filename (preserving user's upload name), file size (for storage tracking and validation), content type (MIME type for proper rendering), and storage URL (location of the uploaded file). Optional dimension fields (width and height) enhance display capabilities when available.

The parent article relationship is established through the articleId path parameter rather than in the request body, ensuring proper context scoping and authorization validation. System-managed fields like id, created_at, and deleted_at are automatically generated by the database and are not accepted in creation requests.

Validation rules enforce that file_size does not exceed the 10 MB limit, content_type matches allowed image formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), and storage_url points to a valid, accessible image resource.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of the file attachment.

This UUID uniquely identifies this specific file attachment across the entire discussion board system. It is automatically generated by the database upon record creation using UUID v4 format.

The ID serves as the stable reference for all operations on this file attachment, including retrieval, updates, and deletion. It is used in API endpoints to specify which file to operate on.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Parent article that this file attachment belongs to.

This foreign key establishes the relationship between the file attachment and its parent article in the discussion_board_articles table. It ensures that files are always associated with exactly one specific article and enables efficient retrieval of all files attached to a given article.

The relationship is enforced at the database level through foreign key constraints, maintaining referential integrity. When an article is deleted, the system handles associated file attachments according to configured cascade rules.

original_filename.description:
Original filename of the uploaded document as provided by the user.

This preserves the exact filename specified by the user during upload, including the file extension. It is maintained for user reference, used as the download filename when users retrieve the file, and provides context about the file's content.

The original filename is displayed in the user interface to help users identify and understand what each attachment contains. It is distinct from any internal storage naming that might be used by the system.

file_size.description:
Size of the document file in bytes.

Specifies the exact file size used for storage tracking and enforcing the 25 MB maximum file size limit per document attachment. This value represents the actual binary size of the uploaded file.

Must be a positive integer value. The system uses this for validation against configured size limits, storage quota tracking, and displaying human-readable file sizes (KB, MB) to users in the interface.

content_type.description:
MIME type of the document file for proper browser handling and download behavior.

Specifies the standard MIME type that identifies the file format and enables browsers and applications to handle the file correctly. Supported formats include:

- application/pdf (PDF documents)
- application/msword (Word .doc files)
- application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document (Word .docx files)
- application/vnd.ms-excel (Excel .xls files)
- application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet (Excel .xlsx files)
- text/plain (plain text files)
- text/csv (CSV files)
- application/zip (ZIP archives)

The content type is validated against a whitelist of allowed formats to ensure security and prevent upload of potentially harmful file types.

storage_url.description:
URL or storage path where the document file is stored.

Complete URL reference pointing to the location where the actual file has been uploaded and stored. This may be a CDN URL for optimized delivery or an internal storage path for direct access.

The system uses this URL to retrieve and serve the file for download to users. The URL should be accessible and point to a valid file resource that matches the specified content_type. The file binary data is stored externally, while this URL provides the reference for retrieval.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the file was uploaded to the system.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime records the exact moment when the file attachment record was created in the database. It is automatically set by the database upon record insertion and provides an audit trail of when files were attached to articles.

Used for tracking upload chronology, sorting attachments by upload time, and maintaining audit logs. The timestamp includes both date and time components with timezone information.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the file was soft deleted.

This nullable datetime field implements soft deletion for file attachments. When null, the file is currently active and accessible. When set to a timestamp, it indicates the file has been marked as deleted and should be hidden from public view.

Soft deletion enables recovery of accidentally deleted files and maintains audit trail before permanent removal from storage. The system filters out soft-deleted files from normal queries while preserving the database record for compliance and recovery purposes.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.description:
Complete file attachment entity for discussion board articles.

Represents a document file attached to a discussion board article to provide supporting evidence and reference materials. File attachments enrich articles with supplementary documentation such as research papers, spreadsheets, policy documents, data files, or other reference materials that support the article's economic and political discussion content.

The entity stores comprehensive metadata about the attachment including the original filename, file size, content type (MIME type), and storage location URL. The actual file binary content is stored in external storage (cloud storage or CDN), while this entity maintains the reference and metadata needed to retrieve, display, and manage the file.

File attachments are created through a two-phase process: first, the binary file is uploaded to external storage which returns a storage URL; second, this database record is created linking the file to its parent article with all relevant metadata. This separation ensures efficient storage management and enables features like CDN acceleration for file delivery.

The entity supports soft deletion through the deleted_at timestamp, allowing files to be marked as removed while preserving audit trails and referential integrity. Soft-deleted files are hidden from public view but retained in the database for recovery and compliance purposes.

Security and validation measures include file type restrictions (via content_type validation against allowed formats), file size limits (25 MB maximum), and access control tied to the parent article's visibility. File access follows the same permissions as the parent article.

original_filename.description:
Original filename of the uploaded document as provided by the user.

This preserves the exact filename specified by the user during upload, including the file extension. It is maintained for user reference and will be used as the download filename when users retrieve the file from the discussion board.

The original filename provides context about the file's content and helps users identify attachments in the article. It should be a meaningful, descriptive name that accurately represents the document being attached. The filename must include the file extension (e.g., 'research_report.pdf', 'economic_data.xlsx') to ensure proper file type identification.

file_size.description:
Size of the document file in bytes.

Specifies the exact size of the uploaded file used for storage tracking and enforcing the 25 MB maximum file size limit per document attachment. This value should match the actual binary file size of the uploaded document.

Must be a positive integer value representing the complete file size. The system uses this for validation against configured size limits, storage quota tracking, and displaying human-readable file sizes (KB, MB) to users in the article interface.

content_type.description:
MIME type of the document file for proper browser handling and download behavior.

Specifies the standard MIME type that identifies the file format and instructs browsers and clients how to handle the file. This field is critical for ensuring files are displayed or downloaded correctly based on their actual format.

Common examples include application/pdf for PDF documents, application/msword for older Word documents, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document for modern Word files, application/vnd.ms-excel and application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet for Excel files, text/plain for text files, text/csv for CSV data, and application/zip for compressed archives. The MIME type should accurately match the file extension in the original_filename to prevent security issues and ensure proper file handling by client applications.

storage_url.description:
URL or storage path where the document file is stored.

This is the complete URL pointing to the file that has already been uploaded to external storage (e.g., AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, CDN). The file binary data must be uploaded to the storage service first through a separate upload endpoint, which returns this URL.

This URL is then submitted here to create the database record linking the file to the article. The system uses this URL to retrieve and serve the file for download to users. The URL should be accessible and point to a valid file resource that matches the specified content_type.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new file attachment for a discussion board article.

This DTO accepts the metadata required to create a file attachment record after the actual file has been uploaded to external storage. The creation process follows a two-phase pattern: first, the client uploads the binary file to a storage service (handled separately) which returns a storage_url; second, the client submits this metadata to create the database record linking the file to the article.

The discussion_board_article_id is provided via the path parameter and is not included in this request body to avoid duplication. The authenticated member's identity is automatically associated with the file upload based on the JWT token, ensuring proper authorization and audit trails.

Validation rules include: original_filename length constraints and format validation, valid URI format for the storage_url, file_size limits to prevent abuse (maximum 25 MB), and content_type verification to ensure the MIME type matches the file extension in the original_filename. The system validates that the specified article exists and that the requesting member has permission to attach files to it.

page.description:
Page number for pagination of comment results.

Specifies which page of comments to retrieve in the paginated result set. Page numbering starts at 1.

Used in combination with limit to implement efficient pagination for articles with large numbers of comments.

limit.description:
Maximum number of comments to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, limiting the number of comment records returned in a single response. System enforces a maximum limit to prevent performance issues.

Typical values range from 10 to 50 comments per page for optimal user experience.

search.description:
Full-text search query for filtering comments by content.

Searches within comment text content to find comments matching the search terms. Supports partial matching and keyword-based filtering.

Useful for finding specific discussions or topics within an article's comment thread.

oneOf.description:
Field name to sort comments by.

Determines the sorting criterion for the returned comment list. Available options allow sorting by creation timestamp or last update timestamp.

Defaults to created_at for chronological comment threading.

Field name to sort comments by.

Determines the sorting criterion for the returned comment list. Available options allow sorting by creation timestamp or last update timestamp.

Defaults to created_at for chronological comment threading.

sortBy.description:
Field name to sort comments by.

Determines the sorting criterion for the returned comment list. Available options allow sorting by creation timestamp or last update timestamp.

Defaults to created_at for chronological comment threading.

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction for comment results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first) order based on the sortBy field.

Typically set to 'asc' for chronological comment threads or 'desc' to show latest activity first.

Sort order direction for comment results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first) order based on the sortBy field.

Typically set to 'asc' for chronological comment threads or 'desc' to show latest activity first.

order.description:
Sort order direction for comment results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first) order based on the sortBy field.

Typically set to 'asc' for chronological comment threads or 'desc' to show latest activity first.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving comments on a discussion board article.

Defines the query criteria for paginated comment retrieval, including pagination controls, search keywords, and sorting preferences. All parameters are optional, allowing flexible comment browsing from simple chronological listing to complex filtered searches.

Used by both authenticated and unauthenticated users to browse article comments, with permission-based filtering applied server-side based on user context.

content.description:
The text content of the comment to be posted.

This field contains the member's contribution to the discussion. The content should be meaningful and relevant to the article's topic. Must be between 1 and 2000 characters as specified in the requirements - minimum length validation ensures comments are not empty or whitespace-only, while maximum length prevents excessively long posts.

The content is validated for community standards and may be subject to moderation rules to prevent spam, abuse, or off-topic posts.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new comment on a discussion board article.

This schema defines the data required when a member posts a new comment on an article. It contains only the essential business data that the client must provide - the actual comment content limited to 2000 characters.

System-managed fields are automatically populated by the backend:
- The comment ID is auto-generated as a UUID
- The article ID is extracted from the URL path parameter
- The member ID is extracted from the authenticated member's JWT token
- The creation timestamp is set to the current server time

Security considerations:
- The member must be authenticated (member_id comes from JWT, never from request body)
- The article must exist and be accessible
- Rate limiting prevents comment spam
- Content validation ensures community standards compliance and enforces the 2000 character limit

This is an atomic operation - the comment is created in a single transaction and becomes immediately visible to other users browsing the article.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

Primary key used to reference this specific comment throughout the system.
Generated automatically upon comment creation.

content.description:
The text content of the comment.

Contains the member's written response or discussion contribution to the article.
This is the primary substantive content of the comment entity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was created.

Records the exact date and time this comment was posted.
Used for chronological sorting and display purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was last modified.

Records the exact date and time of the most recent edit to the comment content.
This field is automatically updated by the system whenever a member or moderator edits the comment.

Useful for displaying edit history information to users, allowing them to see when comments have been modified after initial posting.
Helps maintain transparency in discussions by showing which comments have been edited and when the edits occurred.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the comment was removed.

When set to a datetime value, indicates that this comment has been soft-deleted by either the comment author or a moderator. The comment remains in the database but is marked as removed, preserving discussion context and supporting moderation workflows.

A null value indicates the comment is active and visible to users. When deleted_at contains a timestamp, the comment is typically hidden from public view but may remain accessible to moderators for review and audit purposes.

This field is particularly important in summary views used for moderation interfaces, where moderators need to quickly identify which comments have been removed and when the deletion occurred. It supports content moderation transparency and enables restoration workflows if a deletion was made in error.

author.description:
The member who authored this comment.

Provides essential information about the comment's author including their identity and profile details.
This reference allows displaying author information alongside the comment without requiring additional API calls.

article.description:
The article that this comment is associated with.

Provides context about the parent article being discussed.
Useful when displaying comments in user activity feeds or search results where the article context is needed.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board comment for list views and embedded displays.

This lightweight DTO provides essential comment information optimized for list views, user activity feeds, and embedded displays.
It includes the comment content, author details, and parent article context without heavy nested data.

Used in scenarios where comments are displayed:
- In user activity histories showing their recent comments across articles
- In search results where comments match search criteria
- In moderation interfaces for reviewing flagged comments
- As part of notification previews

The summary excludes detailed nested relationships to maintain performance in list operations.
For complete comment details including full conversation threading, use the main IDiscussionBoardComment type.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the comment record in the discussion_board_comments table. It is automatically generated by the system when the comment is created and remains immutable throughout the comment's lifetime.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Unique identifier of the article this comment belongs to.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_articles table and establishes the structural relationship between articles and their comments. It identifies which article this comment is posted on and enables querying all comments for a specific article.

This field is immutable after comment creation - comments cannot be moved between articles. Used in database queries to retrieve all comments for an article and to validate comment-article relationships in API operations.

member_id.description:
Unique identifier of the member who authored this comment.

This foreign key references the discussion_board_members table and establishes the ownership relationship between members and their comments. It enables tracking of which member posted each comment and supports features like viewing all comments by a specific member.

content.description:
The actual text content of the comment.

This field contains the member's contribution to the discussion, including their thoughts, opinions, analyses, or responses to the article or other comments. The content should be meaningful and contribute to the economic and political discussion context of the platform.

Limited to 2000 characters maximum as specified in the requirements to ensure reasonable comment length while supporting substantive contributions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was originally created.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime indicates when the member posted the comment. It is automatically set by the system upon comment creation and remains immutable. This timestamp is used for sorting comments chronologically and displaying comment age to users.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was last modified.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime is automatically updated by the system whenever the comment content is edited by the author or moderator. It tracks the most recent modification time and helps users identify when a comment has been edited after its original posting.

The updated_at field is used to display edit indicators in the user interface, showing users when content has been modified. For newly created comments, this value initially matches the created_at timestamp.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the comment was removed.

When set, this ISO 8601 formatted datetime indicates that the comment has been soft-deleted by either the author or a moderator. Soft deletion preserves the comment record in the database while marking it as removed, maintaining discussion context and supporting moderation workflows.

A null value indicates the comment is active and visible. When deleted_at is set, the comment is typically hidden from public view but may remain accessible to moderators for review purposes. This supports content moderation while preserving the overall discussion thread integrity.

member.description:
Summary information about the member who authored this comment.

This provides essential member details such as username and status for displaying comment authorship without requiring additional API calls. The member information is used in comment list views and detail pages to show who contributed each comment to the discussion.

The ISummary variant prevents circular references while providing complete author context for comment display purposes.

article.description:
Summary information about the article this comment belongs to.

This provides essential article details such as title and category for displaying comment context without requiring additional API calls. The article information enables users to understand what discussion topic the comment addresses, particularly useful when viewing comments in isolation or in member activity views.

The ISummary variant prevents circular references while providing complete article context. This ensures atomic operation completeness - clients can display a comment with full context in a single API call without needing to fetch article details separately.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Complete comment entity representing a user contribution to a discussion board article.

This schema represents a comment posted by an authenticated member on a discussion board article. Comments are the primary mechanism for users to participate in economic and political discussions, allowing them to share thoughts, opinions, and analyses in response to published articles.

Each comment is permanently associated with both the article it belongs to and the member who authored it. Comments are displayed in chronological order as part of the article's discussion thread, creating a collaborative knowledge-sharing environment.

The comment entity includes the full text content (limited to 2000 characters), authorship information, article context, creation and modification timestamps, and soft deletion support. The updated_at field tracks content edits, while the optional deleted_at field enables content moderation without data loss. The transformed member and article references provide complete context for displaying comments without additional API calls, following the atomic operation principle.

This schema is used in response bodies for operations that retrieve, create, update, or delete comments. It provides all information needed to display a comment with full context in the user interface and manage comment-related functionality.

content.description:
Updated text content of the comment.

This field allows the comment author to modify the text of their previously posted comment. The updated content replaces the original comment text while preserving the creation timestamp and other metadata.

Must be between 1 and 2000 characters - minimum length validation ensures that the updated content is not empty, while maximum length enforces the platform's character limit for comments as specified in the requirements. Content validation rules continue to apply to prevent inappropriate modifications.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing comment on a discussion board article.

This schema defines the data that can be modified in an existing comment. Only the comment content can be updated (within the 2000 character limit) - all other fields are immutable or system-managed.

Immutable fields (cannot be changed):
- Comment ID (identity)
- Article ID (structural relationship)
- Member ID (ownership - original author cannot be changed)
- Creation timestamp (historical record)

Security and authorization:
- Only the original comment author can update their comment (member_id verification)
- Moderators may have additional privileges to edit any comment for moderation purposes
- The requesting member's identity is verified via JWT authentication

All update fields are optional, following the Partial<T> pattern. If content is not provided, the comment remains unchanged. The update operation preserves the original creation timestamp while the system may track edit history internally for audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and searching article image attachments.

Provides comprehensive query capabilities for retrieving article images with support for filtering by filename patterns, content types, file size ranges, image dimensions, upload timestamps, and soft deletion status. Includes standard pagination and sorting controls for efficient navigation through large image collections.

All filter criteria are optional, allowing flexible query construction from simple unfiltered lists to complex multi-criteria searches.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the complete result set. Page numbering starts at 1. Used in combination with limit to implement offset-based pagination.

limit.description:
Number of items per page.

Controls how many image records are returned in a single page. Maximum value is capped at 100 to prevent excessive payload sizes and ensure reasonable response times. Typical values range from 10 to 50 depending on UI requirements.

search.description:
General search query for filename matching.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching against the original_filename field. Useful for finding images by name without requiring exact matches. Empty or omitted values return all images subject to other filters.

original_filename.description:
Filter by exact or partial original filename.

Searches the original_filename field from the discussion_board_article_images table. Supports partial matching to find images whose filenames contain the specified text. Case-insensitive matching is recommended for better user experience.

content_type.description:
Filter by image MIME content type.

Restricts results to images of the specified content type. Supported values correspond to common web image formats: JPEG for photographs, PNG for graphics with transparency, GIF for simple animations, and WebP for modern compressed images. When null or omitted, all content types are included.

min_file_size.description:
Minimum file size filter in bytes.

Excludes images smaller than the specified size. Useful for filtering out thumbnails or low-quality images. Value represents file size in bytes. When null or omitted, no minimum size constraint is applied.

max_file_size.description:
Maximum file size filter in bytes.

Excludes images larger than the specified size. Useful for finding images within bandwidth or storage constraints. Value represents file size in bytes. When null or omitted, no maximum size constraint is applied.

min_width.description:
Minimum image width filter in pixels.

Excludes images narrower than the specified width. Useful for finding images suitable for specific display requirements. When null or omitted, no minimum width constraint is applied. Note that images without width metadata may be excluded from results when this filter is active.

max_width.description:
Maximum image width filter in pixels.

Excludes images wider than the specified width. Useful for finding images that fit within layout constraints. When null or omitted, no maximum width constraint is applied. Note that images without width metadata may be excluded from results when this filter is active.

min_height.description:
Minimum image height filter in pixels.

Excludes images shorter than the specified height. Useful for finding images suitable for specific display requirements. When null or omitted, no minimum height constraint is applied. Note that images without height metadata may be excluded from results when this filter is active.

max_height.description:
Maximum image height filter in pixels.

Excludes images taller than the specified height. Useful for finding images that fit within layout constraints. When null or omitted, no maximum height constraint is applied. Note that images without height metadata may be excluded from results when this filter is active.

uploaded_after.description:
Filter for images uploaded after this timestamp.

Excludes images with created_at values before the specified date-time. Useful for finding recently uploaded images or images within a specific time range. Format must be ISO 8601 date-time string. When null or omitted, no lower bound on upload time is applied.

uploaded_before.description:
Filter for images uploaded before this timestamp.

Excludes images with created_at values after the specified date-time. Useful for finding older images or images within a specific time range. Format must be ISO 8601 date-time string. When null or omitted, no upper bound on upload time is applied.

include_deleted.description:
Whether to include soft-deleted images in results.

By default (false), only images with deleted_at IS NULL are returned. When set to true, soft-deleted images (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are included in the result set. This allows administrators or users to review deleted content or restore accidentally deleted images.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines the ordering of images in the result set. Supported values include upload timestamp (created_at), file size in bytes (file_size), image width in pixels (width), image height in pixels (height), and alphabetical filename order (original_filename). When null or omitted, default sorting by created_at descending is typically applied.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Ascending order arranges from smallest to largest or oldest to newest, while descending does the reverse. When null or omitted, descending order is typically used as default.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article image.

Primary key used to reference this specific image attachment. Corresponds to the id field in the discussion_board_article_images table.

Generated automatically when the image is uploaded and attached to an article. This UUID provides a globally unique reference for the image across the system.

name.description:
File name of the image without extension.

The base name portion extracted from the original_filename field in the discussion_board_article_images table. For example, if the original filename is "chart.png", this field contains "chart".

Used for display purposes and file management within the article context. This separation of name and extension provides cleaner presentation in user interfaces.

extension.description:
File extension indicating the image format.

The extension portion extracted from the original_filename field in the discussion_board_article_images table. For example, if the original filename is "chart.png", this field contains "png".

Specifies the image file type (e.g., jpg, png, gif, webp). Used to determine appropriate rendering, browser compatibility, and MIME type associations.

url.description:
URL location of the stored image file.

Corresponds to the storage_url field in the discussion_board_article_images table. Complete URL path to access the image from the storage service (CDN or file server).

This is the source URL used in image tags for rendering and for downloading the image. May point to cloud storage, CDN endpoints, or internal file servers depending on system configuration.

file_size.description:
Size of the image file in bytes.

Corresponds to the file_size field in the discussion_board_article_images table. Represents the complete file size as stored on disk or in cloud storage.

Used for storage tracking, bandwidth estimation, and enforcing the 10 MB maximum file size limit. Must be a positive integer value. Useful for displaying file size to users and calculating storage quotas.

content_type.description:
MIME type of the image file.

Corresponds to the content_type field in the discussion_board_article_images table. Specifies the media type for proper browser rendering and HTTP Content-Type headers.

Valid values include image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, and image/webp corresponding to the supported image formats. This ensures correct handling by browsers and image processing libraries.

width.description:
Width of the image in pixels.

Corresponds to the width field in the discussion_board_article_images table. Captured during upload for display optimization and layout calculations.

Null if dimensions could not be determined during upload or if the image format doesn't support dimension metadata. Used for responsive image rendering and aspect ratio calculations.

height.description:
Height of the image in pixels.

Corresponds to the height field in the discussion_board_article_images table. Captured during upload for display optimization and layout calculations.

Null if dimensions could not be determined during upload or if the image format doesn't support dimension metadata. Used for responsive image rendering and aspect ratio calculations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was uploaded.

Corresponds to the created_at field in the discussion_board_article_images table. Tracks the exact upload time for audit trail and chronological ordering of attachments.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time string representing when the image was first attached to the article. Used for sorting images by upload date and displaying upload time to users.

IDiscussionBoardArticleImage.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an article image attachment for list views and embedded displays.

This lightweight DTO provides essential image file information optimized for displaying image attachments in article contexts. Contains the core file metadata and access URL needed to render images with appropriate sizing and format information.

Used in scenarios where images are displayed:
- As inline images within article content rendering
- In image galleries showing all article attachments
- In preview thumbnails for articles with images
- In content management interfaces for reviewing attached images

The summary includes file size, dimensions (when available), content type, and upload timestamp to support rich display experiences and proper image handling. Images are compositional elements of articles, created and managed as part of article content.

For detailed file metadata or management operations, use the main IDiscussionBoardArticleImage type if needed.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and searching article file attachments.

Provides comprehensive query capabilities for retrieving article files with support for filtering by filename patterns, file extensions, MIME content types, file size ranges, upload timestamps, and soft deletion status. Includes standard pagination and sorting controls for efficient navigation through large file collections.

All filter criteria are optional, allowing flexible query construction from simple unfiltered lists to complex multi-criteria searches.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the complete result set. Page numbering starts at 1. Used in combination with limit to implement offset-based pagination.

limit.description:
Number of items per page.

Controls how many file records are returned in a single page. Maximum value is capped at 100 to prevent excessive payload sizes and ensure reasonable response times. Typical values range from 10 to 50 depending on UI requirements.

search.description:
General search query for filename matching.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching against the original_filename field from the discussion_board_article_files table. Useful for finding files by name without requiring exact matches. Empty or omitted values return all files subject to other filters.

name.description:
Filter by exact or partial file name.

Searches the original_filename field from the discussion_board_article_files table. Supports partial matching to find files whose names contain the specified text. Case-insensitive matching is recommended for better user experience.

content_type.description:
Filter by MIME content type.

Restricts results to files with the specified MIME type from the content_type field in the discussion_board_article_files table. This allows precise filtering by file format, for example 'application/pdf' for PDF documents, 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' for DOCX files, or 'text/plain' for text files.

This provides more precise type filtering than extension-based filtering, as it reflects the actual file format as validated during upload. When null or omitted, all content types are included in results.

extension.description:
Filter by file extension.

Restricts results to files with the specified extension (e.g., 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx', 'txt'). Extension matching is typically case-insensitive. When null or omitted, all file types are included. Common extensions for supporting documents include pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, txt, and csv.

min_size.description:
Minimum file size filter in bytes.

Excludes files smaller than the specified size based on the file_size field from the discussion_board_article_files table. Useful for filtering out empty or minimal documents. Value represents file size in bytes. When null or omitted, no minimum size constraint is applied.

max_size.description:
Maximum file size filter in bytes.

Excludes files larger than the specified size based on the file_size field from the discussion_board_article_files table. Useful for finding files within bandwidth or storage constraints. Value represents file size in bytes. When null or omitted, no maximum size constraint is applied.

uploaded_after.description:
Filter for files uploaded after this timestamp.

Excludes files with created_at values before the specified date-time. Useful for finding recently uploaded files or files within a specific time range. Format must be ISO 8601 date-time string. When null or omitted, no lower bound on upload time is applied.

uploaded_before.description:
Filter for files uploaded before this timestamp.

Excludes files with created_at values after the specified date-time. Useful for finding older files or files within a specific time range. Format must be ISO 8601 date-time string. When null or omitted, no upper bound on upload time is applied.

include_deleted.description:
Whether to include soft-deleted files in results.

By default (false), only files with deleted_at IS NULL are returned. When set to true, soft-deleted files (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are included in the result set. This allows administrators or users to review deleted content or restore accidentally deleted files.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines the ordering of files in the result set. Supported values include upload timestamp (created_at), file size in bytes (size), alphabetical filename order (name), and file type grouping (extension). When null or omitted, default sorting by created_at descending is typically applied.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Ascending order arranges from smallest to largest or oldest to newest, while descending does the reverse. When null or omitted, descending order is typically used as default.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the article file attachment.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the file record in the discussion_board_article_files table. Generated automatically by the system upon file creation and used for all file-related operations including retrieval, updates, and deletion.

name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded file.

Corresponds to the original_filename field in the discussion_board_article_files table. Preserves the name provided by the user during upload, including the file extension. Used for display purposes and file downloads to maintain user-familiar naming conventions.

extension.description:
File extension extracted from the original filename.

Represents the file type suffix that indicates the file format (e.g., 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx', 'txt', 'csv', 'zip'). This value is derived from the original_filename field in the discussion_board_article_files table by extracting the portion after the last period.

Used for filtering files by type, displaying appropriate file type icons in the UI, and validating that uploaded files match supported document formats. Common extensions for discussion board file attachments include pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, txt, csv, and zip.

This field enables efficient client-side file type identification without parsing the full filename, and supports the extension-based filtering capability provided in the file search API.

url.description:
Publicly accessible URL to the stored file.

Corresponds to the storage_url field in the discussion_board_article_files table. Points to the file location in the storage service (CDN, cloud storage, etc.). Clients use this URL to download or display the file. Must be a valid, absolute URI that remains accessible for the file's lifetime.

size.description:
File size in bytes.

Corresponds to the file_size field in the discussion_board_article_files table. Represents the exact size of the uploaded file as stored. Used for storage quota calculations, bandwidth estimates, and display to users. Must be a non-negative integer value.

content_type.description:
MIME type of the document file.

Corresponds to the content_type field in the discussion_board_article_files table. Indicates the file format and type for proper browser handling and download behavior. Examples include 'application/pdf' for PDF documents, 'application/msword' for DOC files, 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' for DOCX files, 'text/plain' for text files, and 'application/zip' for compressed archives.

This field is essential for clients to determine how to handle the file (inline display, download prompt, appropriate icon rendering). The value is validated during upload to ensure only supported document formats are accepted.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of article file attachments for lightweight display contexts.

Provides essential file metadata needed for list views and embedded references. Includes unique identifier, original filename, file extension, storage URL, file size, and MIME content type. Excludes detailed information like upload timestamps, article associations, or deletion status to minimize payload size.

Used in scenarios where file information is displayed alongside articles in lists or summaries. Clients can use this to show file previews, download links, file type icons, and basic file information. The content_type field enables proper file handling and appropriate UI rendering based on file format.

Typically embedded within article summary responses or used in file listing endpoints. For complete file details including relationships and audit information, use the full IDiscussionBoardArticleFile type.
